speaker: ronedgar
text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Welcome to this meeting of the Council Planning Panel on the 17th of December 2020. My name is Lesley Finn and I'm a solicitor and I'm the chair

speaker: stevekourepis
text: of today's panel meeting. With me are Mr Chris Young, Town Planner, Mr Ron Edgar, Heritage Consultant and Miss Virginia Wise who is a representative from the community. I would now like to confirm the minutes of the meeting, of the panel meeting of the 17th of September 2020 formally. I'd like to advise you that none of the panel members on the panel today have a conflict

speaker: ronedgar
text: of interest in either of the matters that are before the panel today and also to advise you

speaker: stevekourepis
text: that you are being recorded, audio recorded and video recorded. The speaking time for each person is three minutes and any extension of time is totally at my discretion. Perhaps therefore we could move to the first matter which is a development application for alteration and other works to 54 Alexandra Street, Hunters Hill. This matter was deferred at the meeting of the 17th of September for the applicant to address four issues raised by the panel. Now there are a number of people registered to speak today in this matter. There is the applicant Mr Joe Grieco and then there's a number of supporters. I'm wondering if Mr Grieco would like to speak first.

speaker: joegrieco
text: Sure so I myself with my colleague Dan Eagles here, we're the applicant for the project so we've prepared the development application, the drawings, the reports from access consultants, additional heritage reports. We're not going to say much, we just want to wait and see what your determination is and we're here to answer any questions you have.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: I think some members of the panel might have some questions for you so perhaps we could start with Mr Edgar. Can you advise of any issues that you might or matters you wish to raise

speaker: ronedgar
text: with Mr Grieco? My concern is that the plans that we received in return haven't changed from the previous meeting and especially in terms of addressing the the disabled access. We're concerned that what we have now doesn't improve on the situation that we asked to be looked at and resolved at the last meeting. Could you show us what alternatives were looked at and just sort of demonstrate how the proposed disabled access works in compliance with the standards? Sure so since our last meeting

speaker: joegrieco
text: we had a co-performance who are access consultants run through the space with us and develop a series of performance measures and make a series of assessments based on both your recommendations and what we were proposing to do during their assessment. Basically their summary was there needs to be disabled access, there's no performance measure to not allow wheelchair access on site so no matter what it has to be there. So one of the options was to run it through the rear lane way into the back of the house, into the restaurant. Their determination was that it's not a reasonable or dignified access running through that rear lane where there's rubbish bins and machinery and equipment. Also the step down from the courtyard down to the level of the restaurant for him to get into was 350 millimetres therefore requiring a ramp that was about seven and a half, eight metres long which couldn't fit within the courtyard without complete demolition of the area so it wasn't an acceptable solution. So their determination which is why we haven't changed the drawings was the access from 80th street is the best and only way for a wheelchair to access the site and under no circumstances can we consider no wheelchair access which was one of the proposals which was one of the requests from the meeting last time.

speaker: ronedgar
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS Was it considered that redesigning the courtyard so that you could rearrange the toilets, you could create the courtyard so that it was a presentable entrance and that would provide manoeuvring space and level access through that?

speaker: joegrieco
text: Yes all was considered. They also kindly considered the financial implications of making such significant changes. You know basically demolishing the back half of the building to build a ramp. Other than the financial implications I'm unsure maybe there was heritage impacts as well like tearing the facade down to the building to make a ramp work. We were reconfiguring the toilets already to fit a disabled toilet and an ambulant toilet to the point where it's you know there's a limit to how much work we can do you know.

speaker: ronedgar
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS Did you consider reconfiguring those areas?

speaker: joegrieco
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS Yes, yes.

speaker: ronedgar
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS You could share with us on the screen at the moment that we could.

speaker: joegrieco
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS No, no because it was discussed. It wasn't sketched up.

speaker: ronedgar
text: Okay because I did actually.

speaker: joegrieco
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS The current air conditioning system for the building is also based out the back there so it'd be reconfiguration of the plant equipment. We did have a conversation with the building owner and they're not prepared to support us in changing all of that at their cost because it's not part of the feasibility for the current tenants.

speaker: ronedgar
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS Do you appreciate that the footpath isn't wide enough to give manoeuvring space into the doorway and the gradient of the— Councillor GRIFFITHS We do appreciate that. Councillor GRIFFITHS —footpath is there that you would actually be creating a situation that's more dangerous than not having a disabled access at all?

speaker: joegrieco
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS So we were and interestingly the guys from Co-Performance, their response was even though it's not really your responsibility to make that footpath accessible, it's more on Council than us. However, they are satisfied that there's enough room and enough safety for a wheelchair to get into that doorway from the stream. Councillor interjecting. Councillor GRIFFITHS Which is detailed in the report. Councillor GRIFFITHS Which is detailed in the report, yes.

speaker: ronedgar
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS Oh, that doesn't actually detail in the report. They show a number of the standard sketches of the manoeuvrability, manoeuvrable spaces but they don't show the specific— Councillor interjecting.

speaker: joegrieco
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS Oh no, sorry. They wrote in an email. They wouldn't put it in the report because they said assessing Council's footpath is not part—they can't assess the Council's footpath.

speaker: ronedgar
text: I said that in words but they haven't provided any sketches to demonstrate how that would work and whether there would be any improvement if the door were to be re-assessed or if there were landings, if there were alterations on the footpath, what sort of alterations would be needed to make it compliant. The report is basically in words and photocopies out of the standards.

speaker: joegrieco
text: Councillor interjecting.

speaker: ronedgar
text: Chair, but I'm saying it doesn't show any analysis that helps us to be able to understand how you intended to work. Councillor GRIFFITHS

speaker: joegrieco
text: We can only provide access into the restaurant from the street. What happens on the street is out of our control. It's just that that's the simplest answer for that.

speaker: ronedgar
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS Okay, Chair, I don't have any further questions.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Chair, Chris, do you have some questions? Mr Young?

speaker: chrisyoung
text: Mr Young Sorry. Mr Redger's covered most of the issues that I was certainly concerned about. I was certainly looking for some form of graphical analysis to show that the various options had been looked at to be able to answer the previous panel's requests. The way I looked at it at the moment, I'm not convinced that we've moved forward a great deal from where the last panel was. Chair, Virginia, do you have some questions?

speaker: virginiawise
text: Chair, No, maybe they were just observations that we were going to ask people to get out of their vehicle in a no stopping zone, which is what that whole side is, which is sort of awkward and difficult. And then we hadn't really resolved the physical access along the street and getting past things like the marae from the driveway that you could get out safely at. You can't proceed along the footpath. You've got a great big plant in the way. I just couldn't see the logistics, how you could safely get someone out at that point and back to the door. And there's been no resolution of the threshold junction. You need some sort of slight ramping, I imagine, to get from the gradiating street over the new threshold. There's no notes and there's no reference to.

speaker: joegrieco
text: Mr Redger It's actually on grade. So, where that door opens out to the ground floor, the street and the floor level are one in the same. There may be a slight 30 mil step down, which the builder will address with a slight ramp over the threshold. Again, it didn't raise any alarms with the access consultant.

speaker: virginiawise
text: Chair, Okay, that's fine. I guess my more thing is that we're asking people to get out of the car in a no stopping zone on a corner. And the ideal is actually to come along further to where the driveway is. We'd have to get rid of the morale and all the clap track on the footpath to make that accessible. I don't know who owns that. Who owns that? It's not shown on the drawing. Councillor interjecting.

speaker: joegrieco
text: Chair, Sorry, I'm sorry, I missed that.

speaker: virginiawise
text: Councillor interjecting.

speaker: joegrieco
text: I don't understand. Who owns, what are we talking about the tree or the footpath or the driveway?

speaker: virginiawise
text: Chair, Well, at the moment, if you were to get out of the car, as a disabled person in a wheelchair with someone helping you out and head along the footpath, you can hardly get past the morale, which is the biggest problem in the corner. Who does that? Councillor interjecting.

speaker: joegrieco
text: You've identified the problem with that street in itself. It's a no stopping zone. There's plenty of parking on the adjacent street and there's a footpath that connects the two. So there's no expectation that people will be pulling up outside the access door. They'll be coming along the street and entering the restaurant through that because the front entry to the restaurant has a number of steps. We're not talking about a parking area or an unloading area. That's again, outside of the property that we're considering with this. We're looking at how we provide access to the building. So how they arrive on site is a number of ways. They could actually be local residents in a wheelchair and actually wheel themselves down the street. Councillor interjecting. So the question of access can easily be accessed from the adjacent street. Councillor interjecting. Alexandra Street. Councillor interjecting.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Councillor interjecting. A number of persons who have registered to speak in favour of the proposal. The first one is Ms Heather Cook. Heather, did you wish to speak with me?

speaker: ronedgar
text: Councillor interjecting.

speaker: davidguazzarotto
text: So you've got Heather, Dave and Wayne who are the proprietors of— Councillor interjecting.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Yes, who wants to speak? All of you or— Councillor interjecting.

speaker: davidguazzarotto
text: So we were just here to answer questions pretty much. But I suppose in a brief summary, we've opened the restaurant as a pop-up for the last six to eight weeks. We feel like we've added to what the community wanted. It's been unbelievably successful. The collaboration between the local businesses, whether it's across the road, other restaurants or cafes, has been certainly applauded by everyone in the area. We've employed 12 people who all live within two kilometres of the venue. We are local ratepayers. We've now presented, I think, four or five reports. We completely understand that we need to go through a planning process, given the area and given the heritage nature of the building. We've had four or five consultants put different reports up. We would love to maintain the heritage value of the building and get people in wheelchairs into the building as well. But it seems like no matter which way we turn, we're running into problems. So we love the building. That's why we want to be there. We would—there's elderly people as well. We want to get them into the building safer. We don't think—and it's only our opinion—bringing them back through past bins and air conditioning and past the toilet is the best way to do it. We understand there's some issues with the path out the side or the sidewalk, but we'll do anything we can to fix that. It's wide enough. It's a bit bumpy at the moment. But given all of those things, I just—I don't think it seems to be insurmountable, but we keep running into these problems. We understand all your questions, absolutely, but I don't know how many more consultants we can get to say sort of the same things. We appeal to your judgment to hopefully let us get on with building—adding to the community.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Does anybody else wish to say anything?

speaker: chrisyoung
text: No, I'm fine. I'd just say that I don't think the panel is against the concept of having a restaurant there. It's just trying to make it actually work. And I think it really comes down to whether or not there has been enough thought put into the disabled access. And it certainly doesn't have to run past air conditioning and garbage bins, et cetera, like that, for those parts of it. And that's really, I think, probably the stumbling block, certainly as I'd see it.

speaker: ronedgar
text: It's really a design issue to try and get the disabled access to be effective and safe.

speaker: davidguazzarotto
text: We've tried to put the ramp through the back courtyard, but because of the pits that are out the back, the gradient doesn't work. So, there's the going past the bins and the air conditioning, which I'm sure we could spend $250,000 to relocate all the air conditioning and the motors for the fridges and put them on the roof. I assume we can do that. But we still need to go past bins because I'm not sure where else the bins can go. But physically, we've been told, Jo, Dan, that the ramp can't work through the courtyard. If it would work, let's do it. Let's get the sixth consultant to say that's how we can do it. But we've been told by five different consultants that it doesn't work. If it doesn't work, let's just draw it up and let's do it.

speaker: joegrieco
text: Councillor CASSIDY I think, Wayne, the other thing is that the grease trap in the courtyard proves to be a problem because we need to cut through that to get a ramp in. So, it's a major infrastructure change to an existing operating restaurant that we're seeking approval to actually renovate the interior of. So, I completely understand the need for disabled access as well. We've done our due diligence with the access consultants. Perhaps they should have been on this call with us but we didn't realise that we needed them. But I think without them here, it's difficult to reference what they have put in the report because obviously we engaged them to do so. But as you can see from what we've explained with the courtyard scenario, there is a commercial reality to it. If this doesn't work, the current tenants will walk away from the property and will be sitting there vacant, which I'm pretty sure will be a bad news story for Hillshire in terms of encouraging local business. But at the same time, we have actually made this scenario work through the site entry. If we come back to the initial objections that were raised and the reason we're sitting at this panel, a large majority of that was due to the fact that this was a bar or a restaurant that has already approved usage. So, the disabled access, we have a report that actually confirms we can deliver through that space. Like Wayne, I sort of plead that you actually use common sense in this space to actually approve it so we can get on and move forward. Councillor JOHNSTON.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Do you all have any questions? Councillor GRIFFITHS.

speaker: ronedgar
text: No, I don't have any. Councillor JOHNSTON. So, any of the applicants, representatives wish to say anything further?

speaker: joegrieco
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS. I think we've said what we've been currently thinking and working for over the last two months.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Councillor JOHNSTON. Thank you very much. Well, the decision will be available later. And so, I'd like to move on to the next item at today's meeting. And thank you very much for your attendance.

speaker: davidguazzarotto
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS. Thank you. Councillor CASSIDY. Thank you. Councillor GRIFFITHS. Hi, Dave.

speaker: joegrieco
text: Councillor CASSIDY. How you going, mate? Do you like the house?

speaker: markarmstrong
text: Councillor GRIFFITHS. I like the house. Councillor CASSIDY. No, no. Councillor GRIFFITHS. Oh, they were just in the background, I see it. Wonderful. Councillor GRIFFITHS.

speaker: joegrieco
text: We're supposed to leave now, so. Councillor CASSIDY. Well, I hope it went well. Councillor GRIFFITHS.

speaker: markarmstrong
text: Oh, it went brilliantly, mate, 100%. Councillor CASSIDY. Excellent. Well, they're a great council. What can I say? Councillor GRIFFITHS. Hello, who are you?

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Lesley Quinn. Good afternoon. My name is Lesley Quinn and I'm the chair of the panel

speaker: ronedgar
text: this afternoon. With me are the Heritage Consultant, Virginia Wise, who's representative

speaker: stevekourepis
text: of the City of Queensland Heritage Planner. The second item in today's list is an application for alterations and additions comprising a relocated driveway and carport, new roof, new rear external stair and rear deck, minor internal reconfiguration and new landscaping. And Mr. Mark Armstrong has been, has registered to speak. Now, Mr. Armstrong, perhaps you'd like

speaker: ronedgar
text: to either add something to what you've read, I presume you've read the report, or do you wish, are you happy just to answer questions? We can't hear you.

speaker: markarmstrong
text: You're on mute. Hello. Can you hear me now?

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Yes. Do you wish to say anything about the report? I assume you've read it.

speaker: markarmstrong
text: Oh, yes, of course. Oh, look, I think it's fairly fair. He seems to have covered up most of the grounds. There's a couple of issues there with regard to lines of sight, which we can go through later on as part of the process, I guess. And there's a couple of heritage issues where the heritage report was contradictory to the heritage report we had done and what the planner had considered to be fair. So, overall, we're quite content with the way it's sitting.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Thank you. Do any members of the panel have any questions for Mr. Armstrong?

speaker: ronedgar
text: No, I don't. No, I don't. I'm quite happy with what I saw.

speaker: virginiawise
text: Virginia? No, quite happy with what I saw. No questions.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Thank you. Mr. Armstrong, you might like to stay on while Ms. Trudy Atkinson is a resident who wishes to speak. Ms. Atkinson? Can you hear me? I think I'm unmuted. So,

speaker: trudy
text: thank you for giving me the opportunity to speak today. Our concern with the development is that the construction of the roof on the subject property in the form contemplated by the development application will extend the ridgeline west towards our property. The extension of the ridgeline in that manner has the consequence of blocking our present views of the Skid City skyline and the Parramatta River from our lower balcony, kitchen, dining area and lounge room. Views of this nature are rare and significant, so are of great importance to us. Can I just say, at no time has the neighbours approached us to discuss their development application. We don't wish to be obstructive to them because we generally support owners' right to develop their land. So, we're willing to discuss a resolution to this issue for the benefit of both us and the neighbours.

speaker: chrisyoung
text: Any comments, Mr Armstrong? Yes, I've got one. Have you actually done any calculations or any drawings as to show what the loss of views would be

speaker: trudy
text: from your balcony, etc? No, we haven't. I don't think that's on our, it should be on our owners to do that. We've had a, your consultant came over and took some photos recently of our balcony and his comments were that, yes, we were losing those views. So, I mean, from his photographs and from his comments that he made to us when he was on our balcony area, and I mean, it just goes to, we don't need any drawings. It's obvious that that's, you can see from where the roofline is from our property that that's going to take away our existing views. Okay, thank you.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Any other members of the panel have any questions?

speaker: ronedgar
text: The only question I had is really the extent of that is that, would those views be lost from everywhere in the house or is it mainly from the lower level?

speaker: trudy
text: It's mainly from the lower level and it's that part that looks over their roofline.

speaker: ronedgar
text: Mm-hmm. Okay, thank you.

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Mr. Junior, do you have any questions? No, no questions, no. Is there anything further you wish to say, Mr. Armstrong, in response?

speaker: markarmstrong
text: Yes, we were very conscious of the roof profile when we were doing this design and as you would have clearly seen in our drawings, we went to great extent not to raise the height of the roof at all, just to keep the ridge line exactly where it is. Yes, the neighbor is absolutely right, we were extending it to the west by, I don't know, by the extent of the hip, so it's probably about two and a half meters or something, but also the location of that ridge height has now moved further to the north, which would open up their view, in fact. So, if you look at the photographs that the planner has put in his submission or his report, you'll actually see where the ridge line is now, and the ridge line will be moving towards the left by 500mm, 600mm, something like that, and the reason for that is that it then sits on the main structural walls of the house below. When the house was built, I've got no idea why it missed by that dimension, but we've been able to flatten the roof pitch off on the southern side, and it is now sitting above the wall line of the walls, sorry, the walls below the ridge. So, in some ways you could actually argue the ridge line is now moved further away from their main line of sight. I can't see that it's

speaker: trudy
text: going to be an issue at all. Well, I would argue that point because it does extend out and it doesn't look like any, it's an extension of what currently is there at the moment. I mean, it's obviously on this plan here that shows this southern elevation. Oh yeah, no, absolutely right, it does extend on out,

speaker: markarmstrong
text: but it's also, it is behind the line of those pencil pines that are in those two photographs. So, are the pencil pines staying or are they going? They're staying. Is that all, ladies and gentlemen?

speaker: stevekourepis
text: Thank you very much. We will close this part of the meeting now for the panel to consider and deliberate on the matters. Thank you very much for your attendance. Thank you.
